key_insight: An exponentially weighted ensemble of five deep learning models improved lung adenocarcinoma histologic growth pattern classification by emphasizing the most reliable architectures.
clinical_relevance: More accurate pattern classification on H&E whole-slide images could better support prognostic assessment and treatment planning in lung adenocarcinoma.
method: Trained five architectures: EfficientNet-B3, DeiT3, Swin Transformer, Vision Transformer, and ConvNeXt.
Assigned ensemble weights using a softmax of each model’s Quadratic Weighted Kappa (QWK) performance.
Evaluated on 25,545 image patches from the Dartmouth-Hitchcock dataset with stratified 5-fold cross-validation.
evidence_signal: The ensemble achieved 96.52% accuracy and Cohen’s kappa of 0.9648, outperforming the best single model by +0.0087 kappa with statistically significant gains.
watch_item: Performance was shown on a single institutional dataset of image patches, so external validation and slide-level clinical testing are still needed before real-world use.
paper_title: Exponentially weighted ensemble deep learning for histologic growth pattern classification in lung adenocarcinoma
